key_moments.title: On the first anniversary of the city's first death from COVID-19, Ottawa saw an alarming increase in the number of new coronavirus cases.
The new figures bring the total number of COVID cases in the city to 16,483 since the pandemic started, and 459 deaths.
Ottawa's seven-day infection rate, meanwhile, jumped to 59.1 per 100,000 population from 55.1 a day earlier. The lower threshold for the red (control) zone is 40.
There were also seven new outbreaks reported in Ottawa on Thursday, including four at area schools
In commemoration of Ottawa's first COVID fatality, the city lowered its flags to half staff on Thursday.
An interfaith service was also held Thursday evening at city hall, hosted by Mayor Jim Watson
Although never identified by name, Ottawa's first COVID fatality was a 90-year-old man who developed a fever and died on March 25, five days after being admitted to hospital.
Ontario, meanwhile, reported 2,380 new COVID-19 cases on Thursday, and 17 new deaths.
